analysis:
The supplied PR change is documentation only. In CHANGELOG.md (patch hunk @@ -193,11 +193,14), two entries are added to the 'Unreleased — cache reliability' section.

1. Preserve negotiated preload incumbents through uncertain control transport completion; keep configured catalogs above 128 models usable without expanding cache-routing allowlists or native tokenizer capacity.
2. Select a bounded, demand-driven tokenizer preload set when the verified catalog exceeds loaded-contract capacity, with incremental preload negotiation, an explicit legacy fallback, and fail-closed behavior on protocol loss.

These entries describe code changes that were not supplied (the Go coordinator, the Rust sidecar and the provider). So I could not verify their security properties. The review is limited to the changelog and covers no code paths.

The threat-model areas that the described behavior could touch are the cache-planning sidecar and routing, and the cache-routing allowlist. The changelog states that the allowlist is not expanded and that the tokenizer capacity limit is not raised. It states that preloading is never awaited on inference requests, and that the bounded set follows current Registry eligibility. This does not touch A-001 and TB-002 trust decisions, App Attest authorization (TB-011), or the legacy attestation chain (TB-009). TB-002 and TB-009 definitions are unchanged by this PR.

No threat-model update appears necessary based on the supplied text. A later pass should check the implementation diff if it is available. It should confirm that the 'legacy fallback' does not bypass per-tenant cache identity or account isolation, and that the preload selection, which is driven by demand, cannot be abused by a consumer to evict other tenants' contracts or to act as a timing oracle (T-041).
